references.text: Describes the pillars and sockets of the courtyard gates, with hooks and bands of silver, corresponding to the construction mentioned in 38:19.
Refers to silver bands and silver hooks on the pillars of the courtyard, using the same materials described in 38:19.
Describes four acacia wood pillars with gold hooks and four silver sockets, a parallel construction to the gate pillars.
Provides context for the courtyard pillars with silver hooks and silver bands, of which 38:19 is a part.
Describes the pillars' bronze sockets and silver hooks, using the same materials as in verse 19.
Refers to five pillars with gold hooks and five bronze sockets for the entrance of the tent, a similar construction.
Describes the same construction as part of the completed tabernacle courtyard, confirming that the building plans were followed exactly.
Is the original instruction for the courtyard columns and shows the connection between God's command and the actual execution.
Describes the north side of the same courtyard and shows that material usage (bronze/silver) was consistent on all sides of the sanctuary.
Creates an important theological contrast between the courtyard's silver (atonement) and the sanctuary's gold (God's presence), enriching the understanding of the hierarchy in the sanctuary.
Describes the west side of the courtyard and confirms that material standards (bronze/silver) applied to the entire perimeter.
Is the instruction for the north side, which is later carried out, emphasizing consistency in God's plan for the whole sanctuary.
Shows that silver was used as a foundation for both the courtyard and the sanctuary, but contrasts hooks (bronze/silver vs. gold) to mark differences in holiness.
